title: Recent Advances and Opportunities of Active Materials for Haptic Technologies in Virtual and Augmented Reality
review_question: To review the current status and opportunities of active material-based haptic technology with a focus on VR/AR applications, assessing the role of active materials for haptic innovations and their potential contributions to emerging tele-haptics.

findings.antecedent: Piezoresistive sensors (graphene nanoplates, PEDOT:PSS/PU sphere, EGaln/PDMS)
findings.consequent: Tactile sensing performance (sensitivity, flexibility, simple readout circuits)
findings.quote: Piezoresistive sensors transduce pressure or strain to electrical resistance change by increasing conduction pathways. Generally, piezoresistive sensors exhibit high sensitivity and simple readout circuits.

findings.antecedent: Capacitive sensors (ionic liquid, PDMS micro pyramid, Ag/Ecoflex)
findings.consequent: Tactile sensing performance (spatial resolution, low hysteresis, large dynamic range, repeatability)
findings.quote: Capacitive sensors utilize capacitance change by changing the geometry... It has the advantages of a high spatial resolution, low hysteresis, large dynamic range, and high repeatability.

findings.antecedent: Piezoelectric sensors (rGO/PVDF composite)
findings.consequent: Tactile sensing performance (fast response time, high-frequency stimuli detection)
findings.quote: Piezoelectric sensors detect tactile stimuli by using the piezoelectric effect of ferroelectric materials... It has a fast response time, which is appropriate for detecting high-frequency tactile stimuli.

findings.antecedent: Inductive/Magnetic sensors (EGaln/PDMS, Fe NW/PDMS cilia)
findings.consequent: Tactile sensing performance (dynamic range, low hysteresis, repeatability)
findings.quote: Inductive and magnetic sensors utilize electromagnetic wave change... It has the advantages of a significantly high dynamic range, low hysteresis, and high repeatability...

findings.antecedent: Soft and stretchable tactile sensors (conducting polymers, liquid metals, ionic conductors, carbon nanotubes, graphene, metal nanowires, metal nanoparticles)
findings.consequent: Mechanical compliance, high-resolution, wide dynamic range, multimodal detection
findings.quote: Soft and stretchable tactile sensors have been developed by various designs of emerging materials... Furthermore, sensor arrays capable of a high spatial resolution, wide dynamic range, and multimodal detection have also been actively introduced.

findings.antecedent: Electrostatic actuators (flexible dielectric elastomer, ITO)
findings.consequent: Vibrotactile feedback (rapid response time, high control accuracy, mechanical flexibility, miniaturization)
findings.quote: electrostatic types are adopted for soft and mechanically compliant actuators. They have distinct advantages of a rapid response time and high control accuracy...

findings.antecedent: Piezoceramic actuators (PZT, relaxor ferroelectric polymer)
findings.consequent: Vibrotactile feedback (high-frequency vibration, texture rendering, flexibility)
findings.quote: Piezoceramic actuators... are widely used for vibrotactile feedback actuators which show sufficient force... and a rapid response time less than 1 ms, resulting in high control accuracy.

findings.antecedent: Pneumatic/Hydraulic actuators
findings.consequent: Kinesthetic feedback (large displacements, large forces)
findings.quote: pneumatic and hydraulic type actuators are actively applied due to their performance, such as large strain and large volume change... they can generate large displacements even in centimeter-scale and forces...

findings.antecedent: Magnetorheological (MR) / Electrorheological (ER) fluid actuators
findings.consequent: Stiffness modulation, vibrotactile feedback, realistic shape/texture sensations
findings.quote: Electrorheological and magnetorheological types can control the viscosity of fluids by using an electric field and a magnetic field... provides multimodality of stiffness modulation, and vibrotactile haptic feedback.

findings.antecedent: Shape Memory Alloy (SMA) actuators
findings.consequent: Shape morphology, shear force, thermal feedback, light and compact form factor
findings.quote: Shape memory alloys (SMA) are electromechanical actuators using changes in temperature to generate haptic feedback. SMA actuators are light and compact but can provide adequate feedback...

findings.antecedent: Flexible ultrasound transducers
findings.consequent: Mid-air haptic stimulation (skin indentation, vibration, acoustic pressure)
findings.quote: The ultrasound haptic system is a promising non-contact tactile technology that can be used for sophisticated mid-air haptic stimulation.

findings.antecedent: Biocompatible electrodes (AuNM-composite)
findings.consequent: Neuro-haptic electrical stimulation (tactile sensations, whole-body accessible haptic feedback)
findings.quote: Neuro-haptic interfaces... have the potential to achieve whole-body accessible haptic feedback without restricting the physical limit of hardware.

findings.antecedent: Multilayered structuring of piezoresistive graphene-based sensing layer and triboelectric sensing layer
findings.consequent: Self-powered bimodal tactile sensing (slow adaptive and fast adaptive mechanoreceptors mimicking)
findings.quote: The bottom piezoresistive sensing layer mimics the slow adaptive mechanoreceptors, and the upper triboelectric sensing layer that produces the electric power by itself mimics the fast adaptive mechanoreceptors.

findings.antecedent: Ionic liquid droplets as sensing materials
findings.consequent: Capacitive sensor pressure sensitivity
findings.quote: Ionic liquid droplets have been introduced as sensing materials, resulting in significant capacitance changes and sensitivity. The pressure sensitivity has been significantly improved up to 31.1 kPa⁻¹...

findings.antecedent: Ultrasonic vibration generated by piezoceramic actuators on touch panel
findings.consequent: Coefficient of friction between touch surface and finger
findings.quote: Vibration generated by piezoceramic actuators driven at ultrasonic frequency reduces the coefficient of friction due to intermittent contact between the surface of the touch panel plate and the user's finger pad.

findings.antecedent: Electrostatic adhesion force on touch panel
findings.consequent: Coefficient of friction between touch surface and finger, contact area (micro-scale)
findings.quote: When a sufficiently large voltage signal is applied, the generated electrostatic force increases the friction between the surface with electrodes and the sliding finger pad... electrostatic adhesion induces an increase in contact area...

findings.antecedent: Meso-structured polymeric elastomer plates
findings.consequent: Fast and complex 3D shape transformation (shape-morphing devices)
findings.quote: Siefert et al. presents meso-structured polymeric elastomer plates capable of fast and complex shape transformation according to the application of pressure...

findings.antecedent: Magnetorheological fluid in touch surfaces (MudPad)
findings.consequent: Localized semi-active softness change, natural haptic interaction feedback
findings.quote: An array of electromagnets actuates a soft and flexible overlay containing magnetorheological fluid to create localized semi-active softness change... providing natural haptic interaction feedback to the user...

findings.antecedent: Vibration motors in VR gloves (Dexmo, Plexus)
findings.consequent: Vibrotactile feedback synchronized with VR environment, intuitive HMI
findings.quote: The well-known commercially available VR gloves... embed vibration motors for each finger to provide vibrotactile feedback synchronized with the VR environment...

findings.antecedent: Pneumatic tactile actuators in flexible VR gloves
findings.consequent: Tactile sensation (skin indentation)
findings.quote: Song et al. designed an integrated haptic flexible glove for VR application. The proposed glove includes the pneumatic tactile actuators...

findings.antecedent: Textile electrostatic clutches in VR gloves
findings.consequent: Kinesthetic feedback (frictional shear stress), small and light form factor
findings.quote: The ESclutches are small and light, making them especially suitable for wearable applications. They are variable capacitors in which the frictional force between the electrodes creates a frictional shear stress...

findings.antecedent: Vibration motors and thermoelectric actuators in haptic vests
findings.consequent: Tactile and thermal stimulation (vibration patterns, heat/cold sensations)
findings.quote: The vest was equipped with several vibration motors... to generate vibration patterns during interactions. Heat and cold sensations were also provided using thermoelectric actuators based on Peltier cells.

findings.antecedent: Pneumatic-gel muscles in haptic vests (Muscleblazer, Force Jacket)
findings.consequent: Pressure feedback on upper body, lightweight and flexible form factor
findings.quote: Muscleblazer is a pneumatic vest that uses pneumatic-gel muscles to provide pressure feedback on the upper body... The pneumatic-gel muscles are lightweight and flexible...

findings.antecedent: Shape Memory Alloy (SMA) in haptic vests (active-hugging vest)
findings.consequent: Pressure sensations (compression), light and compact form factor
findings.quote: The SMA springs contract when a current is applied to create compression for pressure sensations.

findings.antecedent: Vibrotactile actuators in foot-worn devices (Gilded Gait, SoleSound, Taclim)
findings.consequent: Ground texture simulation, audio-tactile feedback
findings.quote: The Gilded Gain from Sony emulates physical ground textures using vibrotactile feedback... SoleSound is a footwear system that simulates various ground surfaces based on audio-tactile feedback.

findings.antecedent: Magnetorheological (MR) fluid actuators in haptic shoes (RealWalk)
findings.consequent: Ground surface deformation and texture sensations, stiffness modulation
findings.quote: RealWalk is a pair of haptic shoes that use MR fluids to create VR ground textures and deformation sensations.

findings.antecedent: Soft active materials (silver nanowire embedded PDMS, CNT-elastomer composites, PEDOT:PSS/polyurethane)
findings.consequent: Skin-attachable normal vibration feedback, mechanical compliance, low power consumption
findings.quote: Stretchable and conductive nanocomposite materials such as silver nanowire (Ag NW) embedded PDMS... are key materials for soft actuators to generate the vibrational tactile feedback.

findings.antecedent: Shape Memory Alloy (SMA)-based plasters
findings.consequent: Skin-attachable shear force feedback, mechanically compliant integration
findings.quote: To create shear force feedback on the skin surface, shape memory alloys (SMA) are also promising candidates. Its 1D geometry enables mechanically compliant integration with elastomers and textiles...

findings.antecedent: Ultra-thin conformal array of filamentary metal structures
findings.consequent: Skin-attachable thermal sensing and actuation, conformal contact, intimate thermal interface
findings.quote: an ultra-thin conformal 4 × 4 arrays of thermal sensors and actuators mounted on the cheek have been demonstrated... provides a conformal contact and intimate thermal interface on the skin.

findings.antecedent: Hydraulically amplified tactile pixels (liquid-filled pouch with elastomer/electrode)
findings.consequent: High-resolution skin indentation, thin and compact form factor, output force/displacement
findings.quote: High-resolution electrohydraulic actuator arrays have been introduced... The output force and displacement of the actuator are respectively up to 300 mN and 500 µm...

findings.antecedent: Hybrid integration of soft active material-based actuators and rigid components (vibrotactile, thermoelectric, electrotactile)
findings.consequent: Multimodal skin-haptic feedback (hardness, temperature, roughness), complex tactile sensations
findings.quote: Hybrid integration of soft active material-based actuators and rigid components on a soft matrix platform can be a compromised solution to realize multimodal and sophisticated haptic feedback.

findings.antecedent: Ultrasound haptic system (multiple ultrasound actuators, focal point)
findings.consequent: Non-contact mid-air haptic stimulation (tactile sensation, acoustic radiation pressure, high resolution)
findings.quote: The ultrasound haptic system is a promising non-contact tactile technology that can be used for sophisticated mid-air haptic stimulation... generates an acoustic radiation pressure, generating the tactile sensation on the skin.

findings.antecedent: Multimodal acoustic trap display (MATD) using twin levitation trap with ultrasound stimuli
findings.consequent: Simultaneous haptic, visual, and auditory feedback (levitating volumetric 3D POV display)
findings.quote: Hirayama et al. introduced a multimodal acoustic trap display (MATD) using a twin levitation trap with ultrasound stimuli, which is a levitating volumetric 3D persistence-of-vision (POV) display that can simultaneously deliver haptic feedback with visual and auditory feedback...

findings.antecedent: Air-vortex systems (multiple subwoofer speakers)
findings.consequent: Discrete mid-air pressure stimuli (strong stimuli at distance)
findings.quote: Air-vortex systems can deliver pressure stimuli over 1 m with 90% accuracy, generated from multiple subwoofer speakers... It is a discrete haptic feedback system with considerable force on the skin.

findings.antecedent: Magnetic field (electromagnetic actuation with hand-attached magnets)
findings.consequent: Mid-air haptic feedback (magnetic attracting/repelling forces, vibration patterns, volumetric shapes)
findings.quote: Weiss et al. explored a magnetic field for delivering mid-air haptic feedback... A prototype using electromagnetic actuation produced both magnetic attracting and repelling forces with magnets attached to the hand to deliver vibration patterns...

findings.antecedent: Laser-induced thermoelastic effect (low-power pulsed-laser radiation)
findings.consequent: Mid-air thermal feedback (physical sensation from photo-mechanical effect, mechanical displacement)
findings.quote: A laser-induced thermoelastic effect using low-power radiation was recently analyzed as a novel mid-air haptic system... The system caused a physical sensation from a photo-mechanical effect of the instantaneous heating of tissue...

findings.antecedent: Implantable cuff electrodes in forearm
findings.consequent: Restoration of natural pressure perception on hand, sensory feedback synchronized with forces
findings.quote: Schiefer et al. reported the restoration of the natural pressure perception on the hand by implanting cuff electrodes in the forearm of a subject.

findings.antecedent: Needle-type electrodes for peripheral nerve stimulation
findings.consequent: Biomimetic sensory feedback, precise control of grip force, object discrimination (size/softness), high-resolution microstimulations
findings.quote: George et al. demonstrated a bidirectional neuromyoelectric prosthetic hand which can convey biomimetic sensory feedback and control the reaction behavior by implanting needle-type electrode to the peripheral nerves.

findings.antecedent: Microelectrode arrays implanted in brain (ventral premotor cortex, supramarginal gyrus, primary somatosensory cortex)
findings.consequent: Discriminable artificial sensation (cutaneous, proprioceptive feedback)
findings.quote: Anderson et al. analyzed brain microstimulation for a discriminable artificial sensation... Reproducible elicitations of sensations in the cutaneous and proprioceptive feedbacks on the arm were demonstrated...

findings.antecedent: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) via surface electrodes
findings.consequent: Natural tactile sensation (pressure, vibratory, soft material), touch and pain transmission
findings.quote: Kajimoto et al. demonstrated an electrotactile display that directly stimulates the nerves within the skin by an electrical current via the surface electrodes... pressure sensation, vibratory sensation and sensation of soft material have been demonstrated...

findings.antecedent: Pulsed focused ultrasound (FUS) applied to finger
findings.consequent: Peripheral sensations (cool, warm, vibrations, mild pain)
findings.quote: Chung et al. reported the stimulation of peripheral neurons by the focused ultrasound... Volunteers reported the feelings such as cool, warm, vibrations, and mild pain...

findings.antecedent: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to somatosensory cortex
findings.consequent: Explicit somatosensory sensations
findings.quote: Lee et al. reported elicitation of explicit somatosensory sensations by focused ultrasound-based neuromodulation.

synthesis_conclusions: Advanced functional materials are crucial for advancing haptic technologies, enabling the shift from traditional electromechanical actuators to more compliant, wearable, and skin-attachable interfaces.
Novel material design, fabrication techniques (e.g., 3D printing, microfabrication), and AI/ML leveraged design are anticipated to produce active materials tailored for specific haptic applications.

Touch-based haptic interfaces need to evolve beyond 2D friction modulation to offer advanced features like haptic localization, multi-point stimulation, and shape-morphing functions for 3D topology display.

Wearable haptic interfaces require significant reductions in size, weight, and power consumption, along with the integration of diverse modalities using polymer-based actuators for enhanced portability and wearability.
Skin-attachable devices must overcome challenges in durability, achieve battery-free operation, and improve spatial resolution, dynamic range, and output intensity from soft polymeric actuators.

Mid-air haptic interfaces need to improve spatial resolution and output intensity, address synchronization issues between hand gestures and focal points, and mitigate unwanted noise and safety concerns from driving ultrasound transducers.

Neuro-haptic interfaces face fundamental challenges in developing safe and reliable neural interfacing devices that prevent chronic damage, require high spatial resolution stimulation, and necessitate algorithms to translate tactile sensing signals into appropriate neural spike signals for realistic tactile pattern generation.
evidence_gaps: A substantial gap exists between current tactile actuator technology and the desired technology for tele-haptics, particularly in achieving high-resolution, wide dynamic range, and mechanical compliance simultaneously.
Conventional motor-based actuators struggle to create natural and complex tactile sensations, highlighting a need for active materials.
Electrovibration technology faces limitations due to humidity-dependent output, rapid deterioration from dust, and the need for high voltage inputs, impacting miniaturization, cost, and safety.
Shape-morphing polymeric devices currently exhibit low haptic generation output and insufficient long-term durability.
MR fluid shape-morphing devices are limited in their ability to provide full 3D surface shape changes, often restricted to protruding/recessing functions.
Motor-based VR gloves are often bulky, heavy, and power-intensive, failing to deliver sophisticated texture sensations for immersive experiences.
Vibrotactile vest-worn devices are limited in simulating specific ground textures (e.g., mud, sand) and ground deformations.
SMA actuators suffer from slow operation speeds due to their reliance on thermal conduction and contraction.
Skin-attachable electroactive polymer (EAP) actuators require kilovolt-order operation voltages, posing safety concerns for skin-attachable applications.

Mid-air ultrasound haptic systems are challenged by driving noise, safety issues (hazardous noise levels), interference with surrounding sound-input devices, and insufficient spatial resolution and output intensity.

Implantable neural interfaces face risks of brain damage from inflammation, high invasiveness (needle-type electrodes), and lower spatial resolution (cuff electrodes), requiring improvements in long-term stability and reduced inflammation.

Non-invasive neuromodulation methods (e.g., electrotactile, FUS) can produce electrically tingling sensations, are affected by skin properties (thickness, moisture), and may not provide effective continuous stimuli.
A fundamental challenge for neuro-haptic interfaces is developing safe and reliable neural interfacing devices that do not cause chronic damage to nerves.
There is a lack of comprehensive understanding of the neuro-tactile relationship.
Current neuro-haptic systems suffer from poor stimulating resolution and require bulky equipment setups.
limitations: The review's scope is focused on multimodal sensory feedback technology and its integration mechanisms, acknowledging that covering all aspects of tele-haptics is a daunting task and a broader scope might divert focus.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: AbstractVirtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR) are evolving. The market demands and innovation efforts call for a shift in the key VR/AR technologies and engaging people virtually. Tele‐haptics with multimodal and bilateral interactions are emerging as the future of the VR/AR industry. By transmitting and receiving haptic sensations wirelessly, tele‐haptics allow human‐to‐human interactions beyond the traditional VR/AR interactions. The core technologies for tele‐haptics include multimodal tactile sensing and feedback based on highly advanced sensors and actuators. Recent developments of haptic innovations based on active materials show that active materials can significantly contribute to addressing the needs and challenges for the current and future VR/AR technologies. Thus, this paper intends to review the current status and opportunities of active material‐based haptic technology with a focus on VR/AR applications. It first provides an overview of the current VR/AR applications of active materials for haptic sensing and actuation. It then highlights the state‐of‐the‐art haptic interfaces that are relevant to the materials with an aim to provide perspectives on the role of active materials and their potential integration in haptic devices. This paper concludes with the perspective and outlook of immersive multimodal tele‐haptic interaction technologies.
